items.title: Exercise 6 · two-sided Wasserstein bounds for reweighted Gaussian mixtures

source.anchor: Statistical Optimal Transport, Chapter 1 §1.8 Exercise 6, printed p.44 / PDF p.50
source.attribution: Sinho Chewi, Jonathan Niles-Weed and Philippe Rigollet, Statistical Optimal Transport. Samplinglib's original mathematical restatement and proof expansion; no reproduction of textbook prose or implied endorsement.

items.statement: For every real m>0, the quadratic Wasserstein distance between the actual two unit-variance real Gaussian mixtures with respective weights (1/2,1/2) and (1/4,3/4) at −m and m lies between m/2 and m.
assumptions: The ambient space is the real Borel line. Gₐ is a Gaussian probability law of mean a and variance one. The mixture weights and centers are literal and only m>0 is required.
Both mixtures have finite second moments, as required by the Wasserstein domain. This is proved from the Gaussian components, not assumed. A witness for an upper bound need not be optimal.

obligations.label: Use the signed expectation gap for the actual mixtures to obtain W₂≥m/2
Use the explicit feasible plan to obtain W₂≤m

bindings.boundary: Only the named two-sided comparison for the specified positive parameter and literal measures. No optimal constants, exact distance, optimizer, dual equality, aligned Lean challenge, Bench admission or integrated release.

assumption_deltas.source: Real Gaussian components of variance one centered at −m and m, weights as printed, and m>0.
assumption_deltas.lean: The same real laws and weights are local definitions. The only explicit hypothesis is m>0.
assumption_deltas.reason: Probability mass, finite moments, mean difference and feasible cost are derived, not supplied. The conclusion gives concrete valid constants for the requested comparison, not sharp constants.

source_proof_coverage.coverage_status: Both source branches, their Gaussian specialization and explicit constants are in scope; compilation and independent source acceptance are tracked separately.

bookkeeping: Actual Gaussian mixture normalization and finite moments.
Signed linear mean gap and squared-to-unsquared upper conversion.
new_topology: The literal two-sided exercise is the named consumer of both verified lower and upper proof packets.
